title: Vitamin D for the Prevention of Disease: An Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline
authors: Demay MB, Pittas AG, Bikle DD, Diab DL, Kiely ME, Lazaretti-Castro M, et al.
journal: Journal of Clinical Endocrinology and Metabolism
funder: Funding for the development of this guideline was provided by The Endocrine Society. No other entity provided financial support.
authorConflicts: 14 panel members; 7% with relevant or potentially relevant conflicts of interest. Marise Lazaretti-Castro was marked as having a relevant conflict and agreed to refrain from future consultation for products related to vitamin D; several members report relationships with companies including Mantecorp-Farmasa, Alexion, Amgen, Radius, Ajinomoto and Dexcom.
result: Suggests empiric vitamin D supplementation for children and adolescents aged 1 to 18 years, adults aged 75 years or older, pregnancy, and high-risk prediabetes; suggests against supplementation beyond the Dietary Reference Intake in adults under 50 and against routine supplementation beyond it at 50 to 74 years; suggests against routine 25-hydroxyvitamin D testing in these groups; for adults 50 years or older with an indication, suggests daily lower-dose instead of non-daily higher-dose vitamin D. The Endocrine Society no longer endorses the target 25-hydroxyvitamin D level of 30 ng/mL (75 nmol/L) or specific levels to define vitamin D sufficiency.
